metadata.title: Check the Spec, Not the Vibe.
metadata.subtitle: The Brand Voice Enforcement Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Teardown register: when Claude runs a brand-voice-enforcement skill, does it already know what a brand should sound like, or is it checking a draft against a file that spells the rules out? Lands the carry-out that the skill doesn't know your brand's voice — it checks writing against whatever its SKILL.md actually lists, and the limit is exactly what the file says.

beats.narration_text: People type this expecting Claude to know their brand from training. It doesn't — there's no brand-vector in the weights. It reads a file. So: does Claude already check my brand's voice?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is brand-voice-enforcement, and its SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set in plain language — no hidden logic, no compiled binary. The design choice is honest: what you can read is exactly what Claude runs. The file is the program.

Inside is a Steps section — a numbered list. Claude reads step one, runs it, then step two. Linear, no branching unless a step spells one out. They chose predictability over cleverness: same file, same order, same result, every time. What that costs is on-the-fly reasoning; what it buys is a run you can audit line by line.

production_viz.label: STEPS, IN ORDER
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: Here's the actual job: compare a draft against whatever rules the SKILL.md lists — banned words, preferred phrasing, tone, whatever the file actually says — and flag every mismatch. That's the whole mechanism. Claude doesn't invent a brand voice from vibes; it checks against something you wrote down. This works if you value repeatability; it fails if you expected a model that already knew what your brand sounded like. Nothing outside the list gets caught.

production_viz.label: CHECK, DON'T GUESS
production_viz.caption: only what the file lists gets caught

beats.narration_text: brand-voice-enforcement doesn't know your brand's voice — it checks your writing against whatever its SKILL.md actually lists. Same input, same output, every time. The limit is exactly what the file says, nothing more.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini: my brand voice rules are — no contractions, no exclamation points, always say customers, never users. Give the model a short paragraph you wrote, ask it to flag which line breaks which rule, and tell it not to flag anything outside those three. That's the same discipline the skill runs on: check only what's written down, nothing more. Go deeper: ask the same model what kinds of voice problems a checklist like this can't catch at all — where does an off-brand paragraph still slip through when every listed rule passes?

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to try running a brand-voice check the way a Claude skill would. Here are my three brand voice rules: (1) no contractions, (2) no exclamation points, (3) always say customers, never users. When I paste a short paragraph next, check it line by line against exactly those three rules and tell me which line breaks which rule. Do not flag anything outside that list — only what I wrote down. Then, in a separate second pass, propose one additional rule you think my writing actually needs, and explain why the checklist missed it.
llm_exercise.dig_deeper: Go deeper: ask the same model what kinds of voice problems a rule-file check like this can't catch at all — where does an off-brand paragraph still slip through when every listed rule passes?
